context: Vates Xen Orchestra contains an improper validation of specified type of input vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and perform actions with administrative privileges via a specially crafted authentication token containing an empty JSON object.

Mitel MiCollab contains a not failing securely vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication controls and perform unauthorized actions.

Mitel MiCollab contains an improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command (OS command injection) vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary system commands.

Mitel MiCollab contains a weak authentication vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to access sensitive information using a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content.

Mitel MiCollab contains an XML injection vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands using pre-staged malicious content.

Mitel MiCollab contains an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component due to insufficient file type validation that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to upload arbitrary files.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router contain an OS command injection vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID.

Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains an improper authentication vulnerability that could allow an attacker to generate a web report exposing sensitive information, including internal IP addresses, usernames, and store names.
Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains an improper input validation vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to run arbitrary commands on the affected system.
Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains a path traversal vulnerability that could allow an attacker to access and read underlying server system files via the XML interface.

Drupal Core contains a not failing securely vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing site or execute arbitrary code via the Drupal installer. Under specific conditions, the attacker can use install.php to attempt to reinstall Drupal on the site.

Idunno AntiCsrf contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via object injection. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Optimizely Web Experimentation contains an external control of critical state data vulnerability in its account signup flow that could allow an attacker to impersonate existing customer users and modify Project JavaScript. Successful exploitation can result in attacker-controlled JavaScript being distributed through Optimizely-hosted assets and executed in browsers visiting affected customer websites.

N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the LDAP synchronization connection check that allows an authenticated API user to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.

Project MONAI MONAI Label contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files outside the intended datastore directory, potentially resulting in remote code execution.

Broadcom VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system.

Apache Roller contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions.

Cisco Expressway Series contains a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service.

SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations.

Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted SOAP fault message that causes Axis to load and instantiate an attacker-specified class when a suitable class is available on the application classpath. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash.
BerriAI LiteLLM contains an unprotected alternate channel vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via bytecode rewriting at the /guardrails/test_custom_code URI.

Synology DSM contains an improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.

Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.

Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.

UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability that allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority.

Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-111560.

Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG), Load Balancer, Application Delivery Controller (ADC), Message Archiver (BMA), WAF Control Center (WCC), Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Web Security Gateway (WSG) contain an OS command injection vulnerability. This vulnerability could allow an authenticated administrator to inject OS commands that execute with root privileges when the crafted timezone value is subsequently processed. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-116606

Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder contains an incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability that may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience.

Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.

Google Chromium contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XML component that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a specially crafted webpage. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.
Microsoft Office Outlook contains a missing user interaction for potentially unsafe action vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations.
SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability that permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution.
OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux contains an unexpected status code or return value vulnerability that could allow for authentication bypass.

GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml.

SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN contains a use of single-factor authentication vulnerability that may allow a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls. Successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS and watchOS 10.5 contain an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability to bypass pointer authentication.

WordPress WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window. This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades.

Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357.

Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.

Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software contains an unchecked return value to NULL pointer dereference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

Broadcom VMWare ESX contains an insufficient logging vulnerability that could allow a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.

Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root.

Adobe Commerce and Magento contain an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session.
PHP contains a stale internal request-state vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.
PHP contains an out-of-memory corruption vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.

Microsoft Windows Server Message Block 1.0 (SMBv1) contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution.
SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms contains an unspecified vulnerability in BC-BMT-BPM-DSK which allows remote, authenticated users to conduct XML External Entity (XXE) attacks.

Apache Shiro contains a vulnerability which may allow remote attackers to execute code or bypass intended access restrictions via an unspecified request parameter when a cipher key has not been configured for the "remember me" feature.

SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms contains a directory traversal vulnerability via a ..\ (dot dot backslash) in the fileName parameter to CrashFileDownloadServlet. This allows remote attackers to read files.
ImageMagick contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows attackers to perform server-side request forgery (SSRF) via a crafted image.
ImageMagick contains an unspecified vulnerability that could allow users to delete files by using ImageMagick's 'ephemeral' pseudo protocol, which deletes files after reading.
SolarWinds Virtualization Manager allows for privilege escalation through leveraging a misconfiguration of sudo.

Microsoft Office Object Linking & Embedding (OLE) dynamic link library (DLL) contains a side loading vulnerability due to it improperly validating input before loading libraries. Successful exploitation allows for remote code execution.
Microsoft Windows Media Center contains a remote code execution vulnerability when Windows Media Center opens a specially crafted Media Center link (.mcl) file that references malicious code.
Microsoft Win32k contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for privilege escalation via a crafted application
Oracle WebLogic Server contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability within Apache Commons, which can allow for for remote code execution.

Microsoft Office contains a memory corruption vulnerability due to failure to properly handle rich text format files in memory. Successful exploitation allows for remote code execution in the context of the current user.

Microsoft Windows Active Directory contains a privilege escalation vulnerability due to the way it distributes passwords that are configured using Group Policy preferences. An authenticated attacker who successfully exploits the vulnerability could decrypt the passwords and use them to elevate privileges on the domain.
Oracle Fusion Middleware Reports Developer contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows remote attackers to affect confidentiality and integrity of affected systems.

Microsoft MSCOMCTL.OCX contains an unspecified vulnerability that allows for remote code execution, allowing an attacker to take complete control of an affected system under the context of the current user.
SAP NetWeaver Application Server Java Platforms Invoker Servlet does not require authentication, allowing for remote code execution via a HTTP or HTTPS request.

A vulnerability was identified in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file admin/partials/user_logged.php. The manipulation leads to missing authorization. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.
Rejected reason: This CVE has been rejected by Upstream. Ref: https://bugzilla.samba.org/show_bug.cgi?id=16047#c4

A flaw was found in rsyslog. This vulnerability allows a local user to spoof sender identity and cause downstream log consumers to misattribute event origins. When the imuxsock module is configured with plain trusted-property annotation, it fails to properly escape process names and executable paths in log metadata. A local attacker can exploit this issue by sending log messages through the local log socket with crafted process names to inject forged identity attributes.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the ct0 request parameter of the delivery scripts is only required to start with http:// or https:// and is prepended unescaped to banner click URLs. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a delivery URL that executes JavaScript in the delivery origin when a visitor follows it. An active banner using the raw {clickurl} macro is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone banner-linking page (zone-include.php) does not cast the keys of the includebanner request array to integers. An authenticated manager, or a trafficker with the zone-linking permission, who owns the submitted website and zone can place SQL in an array key, which is concatenated unquoted into the banner-lookup query, resulting in time-based blind SQL injection bounded by the privileges of the application's database account.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, deleting an agency, advertiser, or publisher through affected API paths can leave the associated account and user session active because the deletion path does not load the entity's account identifier before cleanup. A user whose entity has been deleted can continue accessing pages of the orphaned account. Access to data belonging to another agency was not demonstrated.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, unauthenticated request parameters in ad delivery can cause reflected cross-site scripting. A crafted delivery URL places a macro token in the source or target parameter and malicious markup in the referer parameter. Macro replacement after initial input encoding can insert the unescaped markup into generated banner output, causing JavaScript execution in the delivery origin when a visitor follows the URL. An active banner is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, user-controlled entity names in XLS report exports can be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas. A user with permission to rename a zone can place a formula in the zone name, which is then included in another user's Conversion Tracking report. Opening the affected spreadsheet can evaluate the formula and alter displayed report contents.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an advertiser can put XML syntax in fields of its own video creative. Unescaped MediaFile attributes and CDATA terminators allow the advertiser to inject elements into VAST responses served for a publisher's zone. A crafted TrackingEvents block can suppress the ad server's video playback event records and redirect tracking requests to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager can supply another agency's advertiser or website identifier as a report scope and obtain that entity's name in an XLS report header. Submitted scope identifiers are not checked against the manager's permitted selections. The demonstrated disclosure is limited to entity names.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone-linking page can disclose campaign and banner names and identifiers belonging to another agency. An authenticated manager, or a website user with permission to link banners to zones, can supply another agency's advertiser and campaign identifiers because the selection lists are not restricted to the agency owning the zone.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the public conversion-variable endpoint does not verify that a caller-supplied conversion belongs to the supplied tracker. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a unique variable for a different tracker's conversion, causing that conversion to be classified as a duplicate and excluded from conversion reports.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager with access to two advertisers can associate a conversion tracker owned by one advertiser with a campaign owned by the other. The tracker-campaign page checks access to each object but does not verify that their actual owners match. The resulting association can expose the first advertiser's tracker name and identifier in the second advertiser's restricted conversion report.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the Search Agents API of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with Viewer privileges can send crafted requests to manipulate backend SQL queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the patch management functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with Viewer web access can perform administrative patch management operations. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

GNU mtools through 4.0.50 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability that allows attackers to crash mtools commands by supplying a FAT image with a zero sectors-per-cluster byte. Attackers can craft a FAT image that, when opened with mdir, minfo or mtype, triggers a SIGFPE in calc_num_clus() on x86, causing denial of service.

ICU4C through 79.1 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in the x11-compound-text converter because cloning shares the extraInfo block without a safeClone handler. Attackers who control the charset name passed to ucnv_open() in applications calling ucnv_setSubstString() or cloning converters can corrupt the heap, causing crashes and potentially code execution.

A vulnerability was detected in mahmoudai1 school-management-system up to ecec9faaf2fb1a3c5cd096e063f8ef326d09cdfd. The impacted element is the function userModel::checkUserInDB of the file loginServer.php of the component Login Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security vulnerability has been detected in TOTOLINK N350RT 9.3.5u.6468_B20250827/9.3.5u.6466_B20250825. The affected element is the function setLanguageCfg of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. Such manipulation of the argument lang leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

A weakness has been identified in Spotweb up to 1.5.8. This issue affects the function redirect of the file lib/SpotTemplateHelper.php of the component Login. Executing a manipulation of the argument http_referer can lead to open redirect. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. This patch is called 0853d646d615225b35f466a960976d1492b786a9. Applying a patch is advised to resolve this issue.

An arbitrary file write vulnerability exists in the patch upload functionality of StellarOne due to improper validation of file paths. An attacker with admin web access can upload a crafted patch package to write arbitrary files on endpoints with the privileges of the endpoint service. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the vShell command-line interface of StellarOne due to improper validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with access to vShell can inject crafted commands to bypass the restricted shell environment and execute arbitrary operating system commands. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the patch apply functionality of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux) due to insufficient validation of uploaded patch packages before extraction. An attacker with low-privileged web access can upload a crafted patch package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

An improper version validation vulnerability exists in the product update mechanism of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). An attacker with product admin privileges can downgrade the product to an older, potentially vulnerable version, potentially allowing previously patched vulnerabilities to be reintroduced and security protections to be weakened. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in an Accounts Manager service of StellarOne running inside a container due to improper handling of user-supplied input in SQL queries. An attacker with command execution access to the host system or another container with network connectivity to the affected service can send crafted requests to manipulate backend database queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the update functionality of StellarOne due to insufficient validation of files contained within uploaded update packages. An attacker with web administrator privileges can upload a crafted update package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An HTML injection vulnerability exists in the alert notification functionality of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of agent-supplied data. An attacker controlling an agent identity can submit crafted HTML content, potentially allowing the attacker to manipulate displayed content or deceive recipients. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the firmware update functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with admin privileges can upload a crafted firmware package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the system. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper access control vulnerability exists in a privileged Unix domain socket of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). Due to insufficient authorization checks, a low-privileged local attacker can interact with the daemon and invoke privileged operations without the necessary permissions. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

Friendica through 2026.05-1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in item_edit() that allows authenticated local users to edit other authors' posts by submitting their own stored copy's post_id. Attackers can POST to /item to delete attachments and overwrite the shared body, title and content warning, which is shown under the original author's name.

markdownify-mcp before 1.2.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass URL validation by supplying DNS names, bracketed IPv6 literals, or IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses. Attackers can influence URLs passed to webpage-to-markdown or git-repo-to-markdown through prompt injection to fetch loopback services, internal hosts, and cloud metadata endpoints.

wpa_supplicant 2.7 through 2.12 with the wolfSSL backend contains an EAP-FAST server authentication bypass in tls_sess_sec_cb() that skips master secret derivation for oversized PAC-Opaque tickets. Adjacent attackers running a rogue authenticator can complete the handshake with an all-zero master secret to capture MS-CHAPv2 responses for offline cracking and replace the stored PAC.

Grav Admin plugin before 1.10.65 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability in LoginController::taskForgot() that ignores the Require Trusted Host setting when building reset links. Unauthenticated attackers who know an administrator's username can submit the forgot-password form with a forged Host header, capturing the reset token when clicked to take over accounts.

Grav Form plugin before 9.2.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows page authors to write uploads into Twig template folders by setting an unchecked file field destination in Form::uploadFiles(). Attackers can upload .txt or .svg files containing Twig and have them rendered as trusted templates outside the sandbox, executing code as the web server user.

A vulnerability has been found in TAILG Feimeng up to 20261028. Affected is an unknown function of the component Wireless Remote Control System. The manipulation leads to authentication bypass by capture-replay. The attack needs to be initiated within the local network. The attack is considered to have high complexity. The exploitability is told to be difficult. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Ghostty up to 1.3.1. The impacted element is an unknown function of the component macOS OSC 8 Hyperlink Handler. Such manipulation leads to injection. The attack can be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 1.4.0 is sufficient to resolve this issue. The name of the patch is 54fe8e188552977249a084db687e75aee6bf12e9. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

A weakness has been identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. The affected element is the function getLanguageContent of the file src/EditorsHandlers/ContentTools.php of the component ContentTools Editor. This manipulation of the argument ContentToolsUrl causes server-side request forgery. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

A security flaw has been discovered in msaifulcsse Ticket-Travel-Management-System 28b68cea41b3a9eb8d533db992e0b5ba2db68854/15c7bc0b48c263233326bb227fef01efc54c24a7. Impacted is an unknown function of the file bus1.php. The manipulation of the argument dfrom/gto/ddate/rdate results in sql injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. This product takes the approach of rolling releases to provide continious delivery. Therefore, version details for affected and updated releases are not available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Kestra is an open-source control plane for workflows across data, infrastructure, and applications. Prior to version 2.0.1, the namespace-files export endpoint places an unvalidated namespace path segment into the Content-Disposition filename of the ZIP download. An attacker who tricks a user into following a crafted export URL can inject Content-Disposition header parameters to spoof the saved filename or extension. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.1.

NetBird is a zero-trust networking platform that connects people, machines, and AI agents across any network. From versions 0.5.0 through 0.75.1, the client daemon exposes its gRPC control interface to any local process without authentication. On Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD, the interface is a Unix domain socket that is accessible to all local users, allowing any of them to control the daemon. An attacker with a low-privilege account can read or modify privileged VPN and daemon settings, disconnect or hijack the NetBird peer, and gain an unauthenticated root shell via the built-in SSH server. This issue is fixed in version 0.76.0.

A flaw was found in Submariner. In its default Pre-Shared Key (PSK) mode, all gateways within a broker set utilize the same PSK. An attacker, by knowing this shared PSK, can forge an Endpoint Custom Resource (CR) to impersonate another cluster's identity. This enables the attacker to establish an Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) tunnel under the false identity, leading to a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack on network traffic between clusters.

Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.15.0, Gogs does not regenerate the session ID after successful authentication. An attacker who forces a victim to use a known session ID can hijack the session after the victim logs in and take over the account. This issue is fixed in version 0.15.0.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 16.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with developer-role permissions to merge code changes into protected branches without triggering approval resets due to the use of a weak hash function in the merge request approval change detection mechanism.

A vulnerability was identified in philipjscott simple-thumbnail up to 1.6.5. This issue affects the function ffmpegExecute of the file index.js. LightRAG provides simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation. Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via an unbounded PBES2 iteration count.

For a token using a PBES2 key management algorithm, decode_jwt passes the p2c header parameter to PBKDF2 as the iteration count without a range check, and derives the key before any integrity check. Unless accepted_alg rules it out, a token can select PBES2 whenever decode_jwt is given a symmetric key.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded inflation of zip DEF payloads.

When a token header sets "zip" to "DEF", decode_jwt inflates the payload with no limit on the output size. A signed token is inflated after its signature verifies. An encrypted token is inflated after decryption, and with RSA-OAEP or ECDH-ES key management anyone who holds the recipient's public key can produce a token that decrypts.

psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed. A database user who owns a table or view another user's application reads can crash that application, with an honest server and default options, in these cases:

- Columns dropped or added in another session while the application updates rows through an updatable cursor, or describes the columns with Parse=1.
- A view whose ctid is NULL, read through an updatable cursor, which writes past the row cache, and a view with a volatile filter scrolled backward with UseDeclareFetch=1.
- Rows added through an updatable cursor to a table with child tables or partitions.
- A column whose type is named lo, written with data-at-execution parameters.
- A DROP TABLE or ALTER TABLE on the connection while another statement still uses the table's column information.
- NULL key columns in rows the driver re-reads for an updatable cursor.
- A function called with more output parameters than its result has columns.
- SQLTables() and SQLTablesW() dereferenced NULL when called with empty strings for the catalog, schema and table names together with a NULL TableType, which kills the process that loaded the driver and every session it serves.

The demonstrated results are crashes; one case writes past a heap buffer, but code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

When Debug or CommLog is enabled and the log directory cannot be used, psqlODBC falls back to a directory under the user's home directory. It wrote that path with an unexpanded ~, which is resolved relative to the process's current directory. Another local user who controls a directory on that path can make the driver create the victim's mylog_*.log and psqlodbc_*.log files in any directory the victim can write to, or leave the victim's process blocked in open().

This completes the fix for CVE-2026-120066 in 18.00.0006.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

With SQL_C_DEFAULT, the C type of a bound column or parameter follows its SQL type. An application sizes its buffer from the type it was told when it described the statement. When the column had another type at fetch time, because the server reported another type, the table was altered, or an output parameter's result column had another type, psqlODBC wrote the larger type into the smaller buffer: 12 bytes past a 4-byte buffer for a uuid, and more in multi-row fetches, where the driver also steps through the array by the larger size.

Other conversions wrote past the application's buffer as well:

- With Int8As set to a smaller type, an int8 column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT was still written as 8 bytes.
- An int2vector column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT returned unterminated binary data instead of text.
- An output parameter that the application discards by binding a NULL buffer overflowed a stack buffer in the driver.
- SQLGetData() with BufferLength 0 on a column the driver reads as a large object wrote a NUL byte past the buffer.
- Adding a row with SQLBulkOperations(SQL_ADD) on a static updatable cursor before the first fetch, then changing that row, rolling back and fetching it, made the keyset index arithmetic free a pointer that was never allocated and corrupt the heap.

This can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable), and by the owner of a table the application reads.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to disable. SQLDriverConnect() then returned SQL_SUCCESS with no diagnostic, and the connection was not encrypted.

An attacker on the network path of such a connection can read and change its traffic.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A parameter-array execution that fails part-way leaves the rows it has already
queued on the statement handle, and the next execution on that handle sends
them. After a data-at-execution batch is abandoned, by SQLCancel or a
rejected SQLPutData, the next SQLExecDirect sends the failed batch's rows
and returns SQL_SUCCESS without sending its own statement.

So an application that logs the failure on the same handle has its log entry
turned into a silent no-op, while rows it was told had failed are stored. An
end user who controls one value in an application's array insert can arrange
both halves of that.

A second route needs no data-at-execution parameter: when building a later row
fails in parameter conversion, the queued rows go to the server ahead of the
next parameter array on the handle, inside whatever transaction and session
settings are current by then. One variant also writes past the end of a shorter
SQL_ATTR_PARAM_STATUS_PTR array supplied by the next statement.

The statements that run are the application's own, correctly quoted; no SQL
text comes from outside.

Versions from psqlODBC 12.02.0000, which introduced batched parameter-array
execution, up to and including 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC did not check that a server reply matches the query it sent: that a FETCH returns no more rows than it asked for, that each row has the described number of columns, that one query produces one result, and that a COPY, a transaction or the connection ends where the protocol says. By sending replies that do not match, a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable) can corrupt memory in the application:

- A FETCH reply with more rows than requested overflows the row cache.
- Extra results in reply to a FETCH, or to the queries of a keyset-driven cursor, are freed while still in use.
- A key query of a keyset-driven cursor answered with extra columns, or a re-read row with fewer columns, overflows the row cache.
- Replies without columns or rows, or with NULL values, to the driver's internal queries at connect time and in catalog functions are dereferenced.
- A malformed relacl value in SQLTablePrivileges() makes the driver write past a buffer.
- On Windows with MSDTC, a long transaction name returned by the server overflows a buffer during recovery.
- Values in replies to the driver's internal queries are used without checking their range: an empty column name, a parameter count, a large-object size, a function's or trigger's argument count, and a result of exactly 32767 columns. They are dereferenced, read past, returned to the application or sent back to the server as stack memory, or make the driver loop forever.
- A reply that ends a COPY, the connection or the transaction at an unexpected point leaves freed results, keysets or table information in use: a CopyOutResponse followed by a lost connection, a ROLLBACK command tag under UseDeclareFetch=1, or a lost connection while a cursor with positioned updates is closed. Eight extra bytes in a reply also make the driver wait forever for a COPY to end.
- On Windows, a start-up reply without client_encoding crashes the driver, and with MSDTC a failed connection makes the XA library use a connection it has already freed.
- An error message ending in the first byte of a multibyte character leaves the SQLSTATE returned by SQLGetDiagRecW() unterminated.
- When a string value did not fit the application's buffer, eight Unicode entry points filled the buffer and wrote no null terminator, so a caller that reads to the terminator, as ODBC allows, read past the end of its own buffer.

This continues the fixes for CVE-2026-120058 and CVE-2026-120060, which covered other replies. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early:

- In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace.
- A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords.
- SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed.
- On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer.
- Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer.

An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC uses sizes and counts without checking their range, or keeps them in types too small for them:

- A row array size of 0, set with SQLSetStmtAttr() or on the ARD, makes SQLSetPos() with SQL_REFRESH write past the bound arrays.
- SQL_DESC_COUNT above 32767 on an APD or IPD writes before the start of a heap buffer.
- A numeric parameter with a negative scale overflows a stack buffer.
- SQLGetData() of a text value of 2 GiB or more into a wide-character buffer computes a wrapped size and overflows the heap.
- The 16-bit reference count and size of the statement parser's column-information cache wrap, which frees a cache entry still in use or overflows the cache, and a statement with more than 32768 columns overflows the parser's field array.
- An updatable cursor that records more than 65535 changes in one transaction wraps the 16-bit capacity of its rollback log, which overflows it and frees it twice.
- A statement with 32769 or more parameter markers overflows a 16-bit parameter count.
- A wide-character string of more than 2 GiB wraps the size of its UTF-8 conversion, which is then written below the start of a heap buffer.
- SQLGetDiagField() and SQLGetDiagFieldW() always stored the five-character SQLSTATE plus its terminator and checked BufferLength only afterwards, overrunning a buffer shorter than six bytes.
- The ANSI SQLSetDescField(SQL_DESC_NAME) on an IPD ignored BufferLength and copied the name with strdup(), reading a name passed as pointer plus length past its end.
- SQLFetchScroll(SQL_FETCH_BOOKMARK) did not check the bookmark it was given, so whoever chooses the bookmark value read out of bounds and crashed the process.
- Four places in the parameter conversion read one byte past the end of a bound character parameter, and one of them rewrote it.
- Binding a date, time or timestamp C value to an SQL_INTEGER or SQL_SMALLINT parameter dereferenced NULL instead of returning the conversion error.

Depending on the case, the values come from the application, from the data or statement text an end user supplies, or from a database user who controls the size of a table or value. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database
password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own
redaction masks it as PWD=xxxxx:

- Pressing "Test" in the Windows data source setup dialog (psqlsetup.dll)
  logs the whole connection string, which carries PWD= percent-encoded,
  which is reversible, and any password= or sslpassword= inside pqopt.
- The Unicode connect functions SQLDriverConnectW, SQLConnectW and
  SQLBrowseConnectW log their arguments as they convert them between UTF-16
  and UTF-8, before the masking happens. The ANSI entry points are unaffected.

Turning the log on takes an administrator, and MyLog is off by default. The
exposure is the person who later reads the log, which in practice means a log
attached to a bug report or handed to support. Making that safe is the purpose
of the driver's redaction, and these two sites bypassed it.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC frees memory that is still in use, frees it twice, or writes outside an application buffer in these cases:

- The clean-up the driver runs at commit and rollback sends queries of its own, and the reply to one of them can start the clean-up again while it is running. The nested run frees the rollback log, or the list of cursors and prepared statements to close, and the outer run uses and frees it again.
- The callback through which libpq delivers notices could run that clean-up, and close the connection, while libpq was still using the connection.
- Freeing a statement whose result holds several cursors (FetchRefcursors=1, or UseDeclareFetch=1) used the freed first result while the later cursors were closed.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, after a rollback closed an updatable cursor, rows added or deleted through it were counted but not stored, so freeing the statement freed uninitialised pointers, and adding a row wrote past the keyset.
- After a multi-row fetch failed on a row other than the first of its rowset, SQLGetData() wrote at an offset past the buffer the application passed.
- SQLProcedureColumns() freed the result of its catalog query twice when the query failed.
- In a process named sqlservr (SQL Server linked servers), a server version below 8.4 made the statement parser free a buffer twice.
- A failed SQLPutData in the middle of a SQLSetPos() or SQLBulkOperations() data-at-execution sequence left the whole operation pending, with the internal statement still allocated and autocommit silently off, so later statements were rolled back at disconnect. The next positioned update ran the stale callback against a statement that was never executed and dereferenced NULL.

Most of these can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable). A database user who can make a statement fail, or who controls the contents of a row the application reads, can trigger the UseDeclareFetch=1 and SQLGetData() cases against an honest server. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table:

- An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one.
- A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence.
- Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted.
- A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement.
- Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal.
- A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table.
- An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short.
- /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens.
- ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time.

An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i, and keywords and ODBC function names did not match.
- Without a schema name, SQLSpecialColumns() could report the key columns of another user's same-named temporary table, and SQLPrimaryKeys() could take another user's index named <table>_pkey for the primary key of a table without one.
- After search_path changed other than through a plain SET statement, positioned writes went to the same-named table in the previously current schema.
- SQLBulkOperations() trusted the ctid stored inside a variable-length bookmark handed back by the application, and ignored the WHERE clause that restricted the cursor, so a forged bookmark read, updated or deleted any row of the cursor's table.

A database user who can create a table in a schema on another user's search_path can redirect that user's positioned updates, inserts and deletes to a table of their choosing, where they run with the victim's rights, or run an expression of their choosing under the victim's role.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application:

- Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR to a large-object parameter was read past the end of the application's buffer, and the extra bytes were stored in the large object.
- After a fetch truncated a long bytea or large-object value, positioned updates and inserts read past the bound buffer and wrote that memory into the row.
- Hex text with a NUL byte, bound to a binary parameter with an explicit length, sent uninitialised heap memory as the parameter value.
- With RowVersioning=1, SQLColumns() on a table that does not exist returned uninitialised stack memory as the schema and table names.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, bookmarks of updatable block cursors contained uninitialised heap memory, and a malformed ctid from the server sent stale heap bytes in positioned updates and deletes.
- With UseServerSidePrepare=0, calling SQLNumResultCols(), SQLDescribeCol() or SQLColAttribute() on a prepared statement before SQLExecute() read the application's bound parameter buffers and sent their current contents to the server as literals, although ODBC lets the application fill those buffers after the describe.
- The driver named the prepared statements, savepoints, cursors and keyset plans it creates on the server after the heap addresses of its own objects, so the server, or anyone reading an unencrypted connection, learned exact heap addresses inside the client.

Depending on the case, an end user who supplies a parameter value, a database user who stores a long value in a row, or a hostile server can obtain memory of the application process, which may hold data of other users or credentials.

PDF::API2 versions before 2.049 for Perl allow unbounded recursion via circular cross-reference chains in readxrtr.

When a PDF is opened, readxrtr reads each cross-reference table and calls itself on the offset in the trailer's /Prev entry. Nothing records which offsets it has already read, so a /Prev entry pointing back to an earlier table, or to its own, makes it recurse without end.

An attacker who supplies a crafted PDF can cause a denial of service in any application that opens it.

WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.28 for Perl write past the end of the Perl argument stack when parse_urlencoded returns many pairs.

parse_urlencoded returns its result as a list, pushing each decoded key and value onto the argument stack without first extending the stack to fit them. parse_urlencoded_arrayref returns an array reference and is not affected.

A remote client that sends a query string or request body with many pairs to an application parsing it with parse_urlencoded can corrupt memory and crash the process.

parse_urlencoded and parse_urlencoded_arrayref check for a trailing "&" or ";" by reading the last byte of the input, without first checking that the input has any bytes.

A remote client that sends an empty query string or request body to an application parsing it with this module can crash the process.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string.

An application that relies on these checks accepts a validly signed token meant for a different issuer, subject or audience.

The ITE it51xxx I2C driver, when operating as an I2C target (slave) in buffer mode (CONFIG_I2C_TARGET + CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_BUFFER_MODE), transmits response data from the fixed-size data->target_out_buffer inside its target FIFO interrupt handler target_i2c_isr_fifo() in drivers/i2c/i2c_ite_it51xxx.c. On every data interrupt of a host read transaction the handler pushes a fixed 16 bytes from target_out_buffer[i + data->r_index] into the hardware FIFO and then advances data->r_index by 16, without ever checking that index against the size of the buffer.

data->r_index is reset to zero only on a STOP or timeout condition, so within a single transaction it only accumulates. An I2C host that keeps clocking read bytes without issuing STOP drives data->r_index past the end of the buffer after sixteen interrupts (default CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_IT51XXX_MAX_BUF_SIZE = 256 bytes), and every interrupt after that reads 16 bytes from beyond target_out_buffer and places them on the bus. What follows the buffer in the driver's device data structure is data->target_shared_fifo and the remaining static device state, so a sufficiently long read transaction streams adjacent firmware memory to the host.

The same handler, and the shared-FIFO arm of target_i2c_isr_pio(), also declare the transfer length uninitialised and invoke the optional buf_read_requested() callback without checking that it is registered. A target that supplies no read callback leaves the source pointer NULL and the length indeterminate; when that length compares below the destination size, memcpy() runs with a NULL source. Because the transmit path feeds the FIFO whether or not the callback provided data, such a target also places whatever the previous request left in the buffer onto the bus.

The trigger is a malicious or misbehaving I2C master on the same bus (for example a compromised application processor or a rogue device on an exposed I2C bus); no software privilege on the victim is required and the handler runs in the target's kernel/firmware context. The disclosed bytes are not attacker-chosen, but their extent is: the host controls how long the transaction runs and therefore how far past the buffer the driver reads.

This is the read-direction counterpart of CVE-2026-14986, which closed the write direction of the same routine without adding the matching bound on the read path.
